cards.ja: 陶器のマグ（ハロ・デ・バロ）
取っ手
縁（ふち）
湯気
ピロンシージョ（円すい形の黒砂糖）
シナモン
パン・デ・ジェマ（卵黄のパン）

cards.en: the hot chocolate made with water
cards.ja: 水で作るホットチョコレート（チョコラテ・デ・アグア）
cards.glossEn: the hot chocolate made with water

cards.ja: フォンダ（小さな食堂）
市場の売り場
ベンチ
50ペソ札
小銭
ぬるい
ゆっくり、少しずつ

cards.en: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
cards.ja: あまり甘くないのがよければ、ピロンシージョなしで頼んでね。
cards.glossEn: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.

cards.en: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
cards.ja: 取っ手を持って。マグのふちは絶対に持たないでね。
cards.glossEn: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.

cards.en: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
cards.ja: まだ触らないで。湯気が出なくなるまで待ってね。
cards.glossEn: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.

cards.en: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
cards.ja: ゆっくり少しずつ味わってね。陶器の器は熱を保つから。
cards.glossEn: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.

cards.en: Greet her first and speak to her formally.
cards.ja: まずあいさつして、それから丁寧な言葉で話しかけてね。
cards.glossEn: Greet her first and speak to her formally.

cards.en: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
cards.ja: いくらか聞いて、50ペソ札で払ってね。
cards.glossEn: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.

cards.en: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
cards.ja: おはようございます、ドニャ・エウストリア。カフェ・デ・オジャを一杯いただけますか。
cards.glossEn: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?

cards.en: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
cards.ja: ソフィならできるよ。私はここのベンチで待ってるね。
cards.glossEn: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.

reader.en: Aunt Carmen and her niece Sofi, 15 years old, arrive early at a small eatery in the Oaxaca market.
reader.ja: カルメンおばさんと姪のソフィ（15歳）は、朝早くオアハカの市場にある小さな食堂（フォンダ）に着きます。
reader.glossEn: Aunt Carmen and her niece Sofi, 15 years old, arrive early at a small eatery in the Oaxaca market.

reader.en: Doña Eustolia's stall is at the back, and she serves the café de olla very hot in a clay mug.
reader.ja: ドニャ・エウストリアの売り場は市場の奥にあり、彼女はカフェ・デ・オジャを陶器のマグに入れ、とても熱い状態で出します。
reader.glossEn: Doña Eustolia's stall is at the back, and she serves the café de olla very hot in a clay mug.

reader.en: Carmen wants Sofi to order alone for the first time, so she coaches her on the eatery's bench.
reader.ja: カルメンはソフィに初めて一人で注文してほしいので、食堂のベンチでやり方を教えます。
reader.glossEn: Carmen wants Sofi to order alone for the first time, so she coaches her on the eatery's bench.

reader.en: Carmen: Greet her first and speak to her formally.
reader.ja: カルメン：まずあいさつして、それから丁寧な言葉で話しかけてね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Greet her first and speak to her formally.

reader.en: Carmen: Say it like this: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?
reader.ja: カルメン：こう言ってね。「おはようございます、ドニャ・エウストリア。カフェ・デ・オジャを一杯いただけますか。」
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Say it like this: Good morning, doña Eustolia, may I have a café de olla?

reader.en: Sofi asks if the coffee is very sweet, and Carmen explains that doña Eustolia makes it with piloncillo and cinnamon.
reader.ja: ソフィがそのコーヒーはとても甘いのかとたずねると、カルメンは、ドニャ・エウストリアはピロンシージョ（円すい形の黒砂糖）とシナモンで作っていると説明します。
reader.glossEn: Sofi asks if the coffee is very sweet, and Carmen explains that doña Eustolia makes it with piloncillo and cinnamon.

reader.en: Carmen: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.
reader.ja: カルメン：あまり甘くないのがよければ、ピロンシージョなしで頼んでね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Order it without piloncillo if you don't want it so sweet.

reader.en: Carmen: If you'd rather have something else, order a hot chocolate made with water, which is also really good.
reader.ja: カルメン：ほかのものがよければ、水で作るホットチョコレート（チョコラテ・デ・アグア）を頼んでね。それもすごくおいしいから。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: If you'd rather have something else, order a hot chocolate made with water, which is also really good.

reader.en: Carmen: Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it with the coffee.
reader.ja: カルメン：パン・デ・ジェマ（卵黄のパン）を選んで、コーヒーといっしょにドニャ・エウストリアに頼んでね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Pick a pan de yema and ask doña Eustolia for it with the coffee.

reader.en: Carmen: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.
reader.ja: カルメン：いくらか聞いて、50ペソ札で払ってね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Ask her how much it is and pay her with the 50-peso bill.

reader.en: Carmen: If she gives you coins as change, put them away in your pants pocket.
reader.ja: カルメン：おつりに小銭をもらったら、ズボンのポケットにしまってね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: If she gives you coins as change, put them away in your pants pocket.

reader.en: Carmen: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.
reader.ja: カルメン：取っ手を持って。マグのふちは絶対に持たないでね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Hold it by the handle, never by the rim.

reader.en: Carmen: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.
reader.ja: カルメン：まだ触らないで。湯気が出なくなるまで待ってね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Don't touch it yet; wait until it stops steaming.

reader.en: Carmen: If it's still very hot, leave it on the table until it's lukewarm.
reader.ja: カルメン：まだすごく熱かったら、ぬるくなるまでテーブルに置いておいてね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: If it's still very hot, leave it on the table until it's lukewarm.

reader.en: Carmen: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.
reader.ja: カルメン：ゆっくり少しずつ味わってね。陶器の器は熱を保つから。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: Taste it slowly, because the clay holds the heat.

reader.en: Carmen: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.
reader.ja: カルメン：ソフィならできるよ。私はここのベンチで待ってるね。
reader.glossEn: Carmen: You've got this, I'll wait for you here on the bench.

reader.en: Sofi walks to the stall alone, greets doña Eustolia and orders her café de olla with her pan de yema.
reader.ja: ソフィは一人で売り場まで歩いていき、ドニャ・エウストリアにあいさつして、カフェ・デ・オジャとパン・デ・ジェマを注文します。
reader.glossEn: Sofi walks to the stall alone, greets doña Eustolia and orders her café de olla with her pan de yema.

reader.en: Minutes later, Sofi comes back to the bench holding the mug firmly by the handle, with her bread in her other hand.
reader.ja: 数分後、ソフィはマグの取っ手をしっかり持ち、もう片方の手にパンを持って、ベンチに戻ってきます。
reader.glossEn: Minutes later, Sofi comes back to the bench holding the mug firmly by the handle, with her bread in her other hand.

speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: あなたはソフィのおばさん（またはおじさん）です。AIは15歳の姪のソフィです。ソフィが一人でカフェ・デ・オジャと甘いパン（この場面ではパン・デ・ジェマ）を注文できるように、「ピロンシージョなしで頼んでね」「取っ手を持ってね」「まだ触らないでね」のような短い指示で教えてあげてください。
issues: Archive lessons[2] diverges from the Spanish source (hot cocoa at a generic café, no Oaxaca, no Carmen/Sofi/doña Eustolia, no pan de yema, no 50-peso bill, Adult/Teen/Staff speakers); not reused.
Card order follows the Spanish words array: 15 terms then 8 phrases; all glossEn values equal the exact English source rows.
Reader has 18 rows; Carmen rows keep the 'カルメン：' marker, narration rows have no speaker label; Sofi has no spoken Reader line.
Spanish usted has no direct Japanese equivalent; 'speak to her formally' is rendered 丁寧な言葉で話しかけて; reviewer should decide between 敬語 and 丁寧語 for a 15-year-old learner.
Carmen's lines to her niece use casual ～てね/～ないでね; the line to doña Eustolia uses polite いただけますか; reviewer to confirm tone.
The Spanish object-pronoun command grammar focus has no Japanese equivalent; the speaking goal teaches the same commands without pronoun morphology.

ドニャ is a draft katakana choice for doña; qualified review should choose the title's transliteration. Mexican food and locale names remain in katakana with English source anchors (ピロンシージョ, パン・デ・ジェマ, チョコラテ・デ・アグア, フォンダ).
The clay mug is drafted as 陶器のマグ（ハロ・デ・バロ）; qualified review should check material specificity and the Spanish name's katakana form. The market stall is drafted as 売り場, not a street cart.
'Taste it slowly' is drafted as ゆっくり少しずつ味わって and 'clay holds heat' as 陶器の器は熱を保つ. The draft adds no medical or injury claims.
The source speaking goal names pan dulce, while the specific Reader scene names pan de yema; the draft goal keeps both scopes visible for qualified source review.
Reader 13–14 keep the source's steam-stops and lukewarm waiting conditions; Reader 17–18 keep the source outcome that Sofi orders and returns, with nothing invented.
Unapproved draft: qualified Japanese review is required before any release, audio, saved-item or progress gate; Write-mode inputs were not authored.
